beats.spoken: What has to be true when a tube says “with ingredient X”?
In the EU, Regulation 655 from 2013 covers this under truthfulness. If a product is said to contain a specific ingredient, that ingredient has to be deliberately present. A stray trace isn't enough.
The second rule: the properties of one ingredient must not suggest the whole product has them, if that isn't the case. And opinions must not be presented as verified claims.

If a maker wants to claim that property for the product anyway, they need adequate and verifiable evidence. The regulation gives an example: proof of an effective concentration of the ingredient in the product.

Behind it all is Article 20 of the EU cosmetics regulation. Text, names and pictures must not imply characteristics or functions a product doesn't have. That covers labelling, making products available on the market, and advertising.

rows.text: applies to text, names and pictures

beats.spoken: For you, that means: look for the named ingredient in the ingredient list. And read “with X” as a hint about an ingredient, not as a promise about your skin.
Check first, then believe. Beauty knowledge, clearly explained: follow Dewlane.
